decision: BUDGET SETTLED AT MEASURED SCALE - $207.31 HARD STOP
why_this_record_exists: Four blocking decisions (D1-D4) were open after refinement round 1. Three were resolved by measurement rather than by choice, which is why the figure moved from a $136.31 waiver to a $207.31 ceiling. Every component below is measured or sourced; none is an estimate.

corpus_transcription.provenance: rate SOURCED AND DATED from deepgram.com/pricing 2026-10-15, not derived from the forecast. The figure was correct all along; only its provenance was CUT30-era course material.

units.note: DECLARED SIZE WAS A SENTINEL. Real size is 1.50 GiB, not 2 GiB.

keyterm_prompting.justification: A/B measured, not assumed. $0.761 spent on one 68-min unit transcribed twice, identical audio and parameters, keyterm the only variable. Result: 'Rohan' correct 12 -> 16, 'Ron' mangled 4 -> 3, 'Nothing Held Back' correct 0 -> 1, programme-name mangled variants 2 -> 1, word count 15349 -> 15347. No term lost, no words dropped.
keyterm_prompting.deciding_argument: SEARCHABILITY, not accuracy. The corpus spells its own programme name 'Nothing Elbach' without the hint, so Ctrl+F 'Nothing Held Back' returns nothing. A vault that cannot be searched by its own subject is not the deliverable.
keyterm_prompting.implementation_note: Per unit. The keyterm list is derived from that unit's media.name and topic - capitalised content words, stop-words and brand tokens removed, nothing invented. topic strings in manifest-v3.json are normalised to LOWERCASE, so capitalisation must come from media.name; reading topic yields an empty list and the feature silently no-ops.

loss_allowance.rationale: Sized against the worst-case request count. The sync fallback at SYNC_SEG_SEC=600 produces ~3,611 requests at $0.043 each. A 1% failure rate costs $1.55; a 5% rate costs $7.76. $10 covers 5% with margin. A larger figure would imply a failure rate nobody believes.

credit_position.why_not_verifiable: GET /v1/balances returns 404 and the project-scoped variants return 403 INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS. The key is deliberately scoped away from billing, so the balance is not observable through this credential. Recorded as operator-reported, never as measured.
credit_position.consequence_that_IS_in_our_favour: With no card attached, exhausting the credit returns HTTP 402 and processing halts. That is a HARD, VENDOR-ENFORCED stop, which is strictly stronger than SPEND_HARD_STOP_USD - our own code, which can be wrong. The 402 is the safety system; the ledger is the refinement. No budget bug in our accounting can become a real bill.
credit_position.funding_split: Not an engineering concern. The operator determines which account carries which portion.

other_decisions_closed_this_round.D2_price: CLOSED - $0.0043/min sourced and dated. The circular RATE = FORECAST/35013 is gone. Also proven from the same page: TRUE PER-SECOND BILLING, no per-request minimum, no rounding - which withdrew round 1's $151.01 overspend finding as a ceil artifact.
other_decisions_closed_this_round.D3_channels: CLOSED - every stereo file measured is DUAL-MONO (2 of 3 bit-identical, difference -inf). No per-participant channel separation exists. -ac 1 is lossless and worth $26.98. Applied PER FILE via the (L-R) difference signal, not corpus-wide, so a per-participant file anywhere is detected and preserved. Rev 1 had quoted a $150.56 worst-case exposure; measured, only 17.9% of minutes are stereo.

standing_conditions: Budget is spent against MEASURED duration, never a planning estimate.
Forecast and actual spend are recorded separately in every report.
Receipts are written PER UNIT as the run proceeds, never batched at the end.
Work STOPS at $207.31. There is no auto-recharge: no card is on file, so the credit is finite and the 402 is the stop.

not_affected.compute: Azure VM remains under operator-decision-compute-azure-2026-10-14.json, drawing on Azure signup credit. Unchanged.
not_affected.other_vendors: Still not waived. Nothing outside Deepgram STT and the Azure compute box is authorised.
